name: Schedules 13D / 13G
use_case: Beneficial ownership above 5%, activist/passive event monitor.
limitations: Text extraction varies; amendments require careful event state tracking.

name: Form 13F Data Sets
use_case: Institutional holdings, position changes, clone portfolios, crowdedness.
limitations: Delayed snapshots; no intraperiod trades; long US-listed holdings focus.

name: Insider Transactions Data Sets / Forms 3, 4, 5
use_case: Insider buys/sells, cluster buying, officer/director conviction.
limitations: Transaction intent is context-dependent; plans and grants need filtering.

name: USAspending API
use_case: Federal contract/grant awards and government demand beneficiaries.
limitations: Recipient-to-listed-parent mapping is non-trivial and must be audited.

name: Commitments of Traders
use_case: Macro futures positioning, managed money trend/extreme percentiles.
limitations: Aggregate futures positioning; not single-fund or issuer-level data.

name: Form N-PORT Data Sets
use_case: Registered fund holdings, liquidity profile, ETF/mutual fund transparency.
limitations: Complex fund taxonomy; disclosure lag; not hedge fund transparency.

name: Treasury International Capital
use_case: Cross-border holdings and capital flow support by country/asset bucket.
limitations: Macro flow proxy; not security-level trade attribution.

name: FIRDS financial instrument reference data
use_case: ISIN/MIC/issuer reference and EU security normalization.

name: TED public procurement
use_case: EU public procurement awards and contractor exposure.
limitations: Recipient normalization and listed-parent mapping are hard; country coverage differs.

name: Statistical Data Warehouse
use_case: Rates, macro-financial aggregates and flow proxies.
limitations: Macro context only; no issuer-level smart money visibility.

name: Major holdings / insider dealing / regulated disclosures
use_case: Country-level beneficial ownership and insider proxies.
limitations: Fragmented; no single EDGAR equivalent; each connector must carry caveats.
